structure: Part 3, Documents, lifecycle and persistence. Read in full: 10 feature/page specs (documents-refresh-no-js 1 test, documents-reject 1, documents-limits 2, documents-scan-lifecycle 2, promoted-documents 2, promoted-lifecycle 2, cancel-amend-ui 4, amend-resubmit 1, notification-delete 2, pages/notification-view-states 11), the journeys README and 7 journey specs (promoted-notification 1, dynamics/notification-events 1, dynamics/notification-data 1, persistence/api-seed-parity 1, persistence-notification 2, persistence-accompanying-document 1) - 36 tests in all; the page objects for Upload documents, Review your notification (notification view), Cancel this amendment? and Declaration; the notification-actions and seeded-journey flows, the seed-context fixture and the seeded-journey answer fixture; the DLQ event fixture; the Mongo models for the notification and accompanying_documents collections and the outbox event (GBN-AG payload); the backend notification API and fulfilments wire models; the PIMS Dynamics importer-notification row model; the frontend-form, REST, notification API, animals Dynamics and Dataverse HTTP clients, the Mongo and SQS clients; and the synthetic-file, EICAR and scan-status utilities. resources/file-upload/constants.ts and paths.ts were also read because the document specs take their limits and messages from them. Covered: the Upload documents page and its scan states, no-JS refresh, the 15-document and 10MB limits and their error copy, file-type and virus rejects, download headers and removal; the notification lifecycle (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND, DELETED) through the backend API and the UI view states, amend and resubmit, cancel amendment with its confirmation page and banner, delete with its confirmation page, copy as new, confirmation page; and what is stored in Mongo and sent to PIMS Dynamics, plus the outbox, API and Dynamics field catalogues. Claims run spec by spec, then the support models.

claims.statement: Copying a notification (POST /notifications/{id}/copy with the source's concurrency token) creates a new DRAFT with a new reference number every time; copies are not de-duplicated and copying does not change the source.

claims.quote: // Soft-delete is idempotent — repeated calls return the DELETED notification unchanged.

claims.statement: PUT /notifications/{id} replaces the whole record; it answers 404 for an unknown reference and 400 without a matching concurrency token, and an optional actor supplies the organisation id so address-book party references resolve onto the NotificationEdited event.
claims.quote:
Whole-record replace of an existing notification via PUT /notifications/{id}.
   * 404 if the reference is unknown, 400 without a matching concurrencyToken. The
